newsitem.title: UK: Argentina wants end to grain subsidies, Sola says.
newsitem.headline: Argentina wants end to grain subsidies, Sola says.

text.p: Argentina will continue to work for the total abolition of production incentives and export subsidies in the world grains market, according to Secretary of Agriculture Felipe Sola.
Sola was delivering a speech at the International Grains Council's conference in London on Thursday.
He said Argentina, one of the Cairns group of exporting countries, had pushed, through the World Trade Organisation, for the elimination of subsidies and would continue to do so.
He highlighted the EU and the U.S. as subsidisers of grain trade.
"We continue to work actively in the Cairns Group towards total abolition of this practice, of which we have been a victim for many years," Sola said.

Argentina was well placed to compete in a more open global market, Sola said. Argentine conditions had "allowed producers to adapt readily to unequal conditions in a world market dominated by subsidies and protectionist policies," he said.
"Proof of this is the significant expansion of oilseed production during the 1980s, following a rise in demand for protein meal for livestock feeding," Sola said.
Improved efficiency meant that grain production reached a record 53.4 million tonnes in 1996/97, Sola said, despite bad weather in some of the country's agricultural areas.

Sola stressed the lack of government interference in the grain trade. "Argentina's grain trade developed without any kind of government intervention affecting pricing, thus allowing free interplay of supply and demand, and encouraging free decision making by producers," he said.
